recentItems.title: What disappearing birds are trying to tell us | Pippin Frisbie-Calder | TEDxBatonRouge
recentItems.description:
Nearly three billion birds have disappeared from North America in the past fifty years. The data is overwhelming, and somehow it isn't moving us fast enough. Pippin Frisbie-Calder has spent her career asking why we struggle to act on what we already know, and what art can do about it. Working at the intersection of printmaking, ecological science, and advocacy, she uses large-scale installations and collaborations with researchers to transform statistics about species loss into experiences people can feel. Her talk opens with a sound that no longer exists, the call of the extinct Ivory-billed Woodpecker, and builds a case for art as one of the most underused tools in the climate response.

Pippin Frisbie-Calder is a visual artist and environmental printmaker based in Louisiana whose large-scale woodcuts, silkscreen prints, and immersive installations bring the threatened ecosystems of the Gulf South into galleries, classrooms, and public spaces. She collaborates closely with scientists and conservation organizations, including the Audubon Society, to translate research into art that is both visually compelling and urgently relevant. Her artist residencies have included the Louisiana State University Veterinary Teaching Hospital and A Studio in the Woods in New Orleans. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to repair a relationship in 3 steps | Pearl Moses | TEDxArden University Manchester
recentItems.description:
Everyone makes mistakes—but the heartbeat of who we are is revealed in the seconds after. This talk invites us to trade defensiveness for courage: name the misstep, own the impact, and take action to repair. Accountability isn’t a public confession; it’s a practical promise that restores dignity and rebuilds trust. When leaders model honest responsibility, individuals and teams feel safe to speak up, learn faster, and grow stronger together. Repair over perfection creates cultures where people can be imperfect and still be dependable. Choose repair—and you don’t just recover from failure; you reshape what’s possible. 

Pearl Moses is Compliance Director at Setfords Law Ltd and a solicitor with several years’ experience in regulatory compliance, legal publishing, and private practice. Formerly Risk and Compliance Lead at the Law Society of England and Wales, she has held senior regulatory roles and serves on the Law Society’s Legal Compliance Bulletin’s editorial board. Pearl is a sought after speaker and is author of Owning Up to Mistakes, an ethics  and culture focused book published by the Law Society of England and Wales. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Data Centers: What Lies Beyond Yes or No? | Ian Sun | TEDxAtlanta Youth
recentItems.description:
Build the data center—or block it? That yes-or-no debate can leave important questions unanswered. Undergraduate student Ian Sun explores what becomes possible when communities can see more of the tradeoffs and ask where, how and with whose input these facilities should be built. Ian Sun believes innovation must work for the people who have to live with its consequences. 

An electrical engineering and computer science student at MIT, he builds technology to tackle real-world problems. 

A sustainability hackathon led him to explore AI’s physical footprint and how better data can give communities a voice in shaping the infrastructure behind it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Problem With Calling Young People “The Future” | Temple Lester | TEDxAtlanta Youth
recentItems.description:
At eight, Temple Lester went to science camp to build rockets. Instead, she was asked to help the boys. Years later, she began questioning something adults say to children with the best intentions: “You are the future.” Could those encouraging words be keeping young people on the sidelines? STEM advocate Temple Lester has spent nearly a decade helping young people recognize the power of their ideas and imagination.

A physics student and Karsh STEM Scholar at Howard University, Temple founded STEM Girl Swag and has been recognized as a Coca-Cola Scholar, Time Kid of the Year finalist and White House honoree. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How one unexpected voice can change everything | Genevieve LeDoux | TEDxAtlanta
recentItems.description:
Ever had an idea you talked yourself out of before anyone else could reject it? After decades in the entertainment and media industry, Genevieve LeDoux knew that feeling well. Then a question from a five-year-old challenged everything she thought she knew about experience, creativity, and whose ideas deserve to be heard. Genevieve LeDoux has spent her career turning imagination into stories and questioning what happens to creativity when we get too good at knowing the rules.

An Emmy-winning producer, songwriter and storyteller, Genevieve has spent nearly two decades creating entertainment for young audiences. Her work spans television, music, animation and interactive media, bringing together artists, writers and technologists to build worlds designed to capture a child’s imagination.

Today, Genevieve is the creator of Star Forest, an animated musical universe inspired by nature, music and the wonderfully unconventional ways children see the world. Through her work, she continues to explore where original ideas come from and what allows them to survive long enough to become real. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Ask these three questions about new tourist developments | Kimberly Clarke | TEDxLogan Circle
recentItems.description: Cities around the world are investing billions of dollars to attract tourists by building stadiums, resorts, convention centers, and entertainment districts, including many projects emerging across the Washington, D.C. region. Yet, places that pursue the same strategy often see very different results. Some destinations experience strong economic growth, new jobs, and vibrant local businesses, while others struggle with overcrowded infrastructure, rising housing costs, and pressure on natural and cultural resources. How can the same strategy lead to such different outcomes? Kimberly’s research explores why tourism benefits some destinations while straining others. In her talk, she reveals the key questions to ask about new development to ensure we strengthen destinations rather than strain them. Dr. Kimberly Clarke is a public policy professional, researcher, and speaker based in the Washington, D.C. area. She holds a PhD from Southern New Hampshire University, holds degrees from Johnson & Wales University, and earned an MBA from Bowie State University. Her research explores how tourism policy can harmonize economic growth with environmental sustainability. Her work bridges academic research with practical strategies that help communities thrive while creating lasting benefits for residents and visitors alike. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Il coraggio di avere Coraggio | Stefano Zaccaria | TEDxSiena
recentItems.description: Un ponte si interrompe a mezz’aria, eppure nell’acqua il suo riflesso appare intero. In quel dipinto Stefano Zaccaria riconosce qualcosa che accade quando proviamo a dare forma a un’idea: riusciamo a intravedere ciò che potrebbe diventare mentre stiamo ancora cercando il modo di costruirla. Il coraggio entra in gioco quando decidiamo che vale la pena cominciare e raccontiamo quell’idea a qualcuno. A volte, proprio raccontandola, scopriamo che altri vedono una possibilità dove noi vedevamo soltanto un desiderio. Da quel momento, scegliere una direzione può diventare una responsabilità condivisa. Stefano Zaccaria è direttore marketing di Toyota Material Handling Italia dal 2021, nel settore dell’intralogistica e della movimentazione delle merci. Ha iniziato la carriera nella produzione presso Pineider, dove ha poi assunto la direzione commerciale e marketing. È stato amministratore delegato di Antiche Officine Pineider e vicepresidente per le vendite globali e il marketing di K-array, azienda toscana di audio professionale. Fa parte del consiglio di amministrazione della Fondazione Giovanni Michelucci. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: When Destiny Meets Determination | Mandeep Baisla | TEDxMAIMS
recentItems.description: Mandeep’s TED Talk explores how discipline, education, and perseverance shaped his journey from a shy student to a practising advocate. Through his personal experiences and career challenges, he highlights the importance of personal growth and self-belief. Recognising the complexity of Indian law for ordinary citizens, he began simplifying legal concepts through Instagram, making legal awareness more accessible. His journey emphasises that education goes beyond degreeS, it is about growth, purpose, and creating meaningful impact. Mandeep Baisala is an Advocate at the Supreme Court of India, with experience in litigation and legal practice. Beyond the courtroom, he is involved in legal education and mentorship, helping aspiring lawyers navigate the profession with clarity and confidence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: La memoria non resta in silenzio | Annamaria Torre | TEDxSiena
recentItems.description: Annamaria Torre aveva quindici anni quando vide suo padre, Marcello Torre, assassinato dalla camorra. Era sindaco di Pagani, la sua città d’origine. Nella lettera che lasciò alla famiglia scrisse di sognare una Pagani civile e libera. Il suo impegno per la città passava anche dal dire «no» alle infiltrazioni della camorra negli appalti pubblici. Oggi Annamaria porta quella storia nelle scuole e chiede ai ragazzi quanto pesa dire «no» di fronte a un illecito o a un’ingiustizia, quando voltarsi dall’altra parte sarebbe più facile. Nel suo racconto, fare memoria significa trasmettere il coraggio di prendere posizione anche quando si ha paura. Annamaria Torre è impegnata nella testimonianza civile e nell’educazione alla legalità. Aveva quindici anni quando suo padre Marcello, avvocato e sindaco di Pagani, fu assassinato dalla camorra l’11 dicembre 1980. Oggi presiede l’Associazione Marcello Torre, nata per iniziativa della madre Lucia De Palma, che organizza il Premio Nazionale per l’Impegno Civile. È attiva in Libera e incontra gli studenti per raccontare la storia del padre e discutere con loro di come ci si possa opporre alle mafie nella vita quotidiana. Ha anche scritto una biografia del padre. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Language You Already Speak | Gan-Erdene Boldbaatar | TEDxShildeg School Youth
recentItems.description:
I was twelve, watching television, when a dancer introduced himself as a graphic designer. I had no idea what the words meant. Then he performed, the screen behind him moved with him, and I understood one thing without understanding any of it. He wasn't designing graphics; he was speaking with it.

He didn't know he was giving me something. Nor did the strangers who gave me free tutorials. Much of what I know, I owe to people who will never know my name.

Graphic design was never a profession. It was a language only a few people were allowed to speak. That permission is gone, because another stranger is giving it away without knowing. AI will hand anyone a fluent-looking image in three seconds. No tutorials, no six years. Everyone receives it, asked or not. That's how languages spread.

Once AI makes everyone fluent, fluency stops being worth much. What's left is who can read it. Every ad, every thumbnail you scroll past decides how you feel before you've read a word, and most of us can't say how.

It took six years for me to become literate in this language, and I am not even fluent in it yet. Here’s a ten-second sample of it for you: a single clip with two cuts. Identical footage, except for four frames. 

So.
 
Everyone will be speaking it. Who will be reading it? Gan-Erdene Boldbaatar is an eighteen-year-old video editor and designer from Erdenet. He began at the age of twelve by attempting to replicate the style of his Counter-Strike clips. There was no one in his city who could teach him how to do this, so it was tutorials that did the trick. Six years later, he works as an editor for people such as Lexor2k, MaNZuuL and fury5k, and has been making videos for the Orkhon Aimag Children's Council since 2024. He arranged the YOUTH POWER ORKHON-2025 conference, created media for it, and organized an event to bring scholarship and education information to rural kids. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Maya of success  | Keshav Sadhna | TEDxMAIMS
recentItems.description:
In his TEDx talk, “Maya of Success,” the speaker shares his journey in the acting industry and reflects on the factors that have shaped his success. He talks about his passion for acting, how he entered the industry, and the joy he found in pursuing something he truly loved. His journey highlights the importance of following one’s passion and staying committed to it despite the challenges that may arise along the way.
The speaker believes that two important elements contribute to success: hard work and spirituality. According to him, success is not achieved overnight but is the result of consistent effort, dedication, and belief in oneself. He emphasises that the achievements he has earned throughout his journey are a reflection of the hard work he has put in and the consistency with which he has pursued his goals. Through his experiences, he encourages people to remain focused on their ambitions, trust the process, and understand that true success comes from a combination of persistent effort and inner belief. Keshav Sadhna is an Indian actor best known for portraying Karan in TVF’s College Romance, a role he played across all four seasons. His diverse portfolio spans OTT, television and films, with notable appearances in Code M, Hero: Gayab Mode On, Phone-a-Friend, Bakaiti, Gustaakh Ishq and Aukaat Ke Bahar. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
